svg.text: LE-01 · Sheet 3/3 · THE BLEED KNOT — how every ring and hook is fixed
Bellowerk Manufaktur · v3.0 · 18 Sep 2026 · A3 landscape · Taken from the golden sample. The technique is the "bleed knot" (also called blood knot) —
a known leather technique, no stitching and no rivets. The strap is NEVER cut into strands and NEVER cut through. It is one piece from end to end.
How to read the drawings:
grain side (outside)
flesh side (rough)
The flesh side showing through is how you know the knot is right.
One slit — that is the whole secret
30 mm
slit runs ALONG the strap
ONE lengthwise slit in the middle of the strap, 30 mm long,
centred across the width. Both ends punched Ø 2 mm so the
slit cannot run. Nothing else is cut — the strap keeps its
full 20 mm width and stays one piece.
Thread the ring, then the tail through the slit
the WHOLE tail goes through the slit
Put the ring (or the snap hook) on the strap, then push the
entire rest of the lead through the open slit. On a 2.60 m lead
that means pulling metres of leather through — that is normal
and it is why the knots are made before the lead is cut to length.
Pull tight — the V appears
flesh side now shows
Pull the tail through until the knot sits tight against the ring.
The leather turns as it passes through itself, so the rough flesh
side comes to the outside and forms a V. That light patch is the
proof the knot is made correctly — it is not a fault.
Repeat — the chain at the hook ends
115 mm · 5–6 V, pitch approx. 20 mm
At hook A and hook B the knot is repeated in a row: cut the next
slit, pull the tail through again, tighten. Five to six V over
115 mm, evenly spaced — match the golden sample.
Ring 1 and ring 2 — ONE knot, no screw
lead continues
lead continues
A middle ring gets a SINGLE bleed knot and no Chicago screw.
The knot alone holds it — that is how the golden sample is made.
Pull it up tight so the ring cannot travel along the strap.
Finish at the hook ends
1 Chicago screw after the last V
Only at hook A and hook B: one solid brass Chicago screw after
the last V, tail trimmed 20 mm behind it, edge bevelled. The knots
carry the load — the screw only stops the tail lifting.
The three positions on the lead
Hook A — 5–6 knots + 1 screw
Strap through the hook eye, folded back, then the
chain of knots. Tail ends after the screw.
Ring 1 and ring 2 — 1 knot, no screw
One continuous strap runs straight through.
Nothing else holds the ring.
Ring 3 + hook B — both in one fold
The strap goes through ring 3 AND the hook eye
before the knots start. Ring 30 mm before the eye.
Check on the
first sample
Slit length 30 mm is a
starting value. Adjust it
until the chain measures
115 mm with 5–6 even V,
and the knots sit tight
with no gaps.
Send photos of one
finished knot, front
and back, before
production.
